An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty or using known parameters of the $B^0_s$ system.

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels, exhibiting an energy dependence that exactly follows a quadratic relationship. Furthermore, we discovered that the orientation of this dipolar modulation shifts with an observed frequency of approximately 94 degrays in right ascension, and a relatively small sidereal-day periodicity of around 291 degrees in local time. In contrast, we found no corresponding evidence of corresponding features in observed cosmic-ray flux levels or cosmic-ray directional distribution.

The ATLAS detector, installed at the LHC, was employed in identifying p+Pb collisions and deriving nuclear modification factors for various particle types, including neutral pions, protons, and J/ψ mesons, from 2012 data. Neutral pion assessments were made at central rapidities for various centralities, while proton analyses were conducted at both mid and forward rapidities. J/ψ meson studies were carried out at mid and forward rapidities with no discernible centrality dependence. The measurements indicate a nuclear modification factor greater than one for pions and protons in both forward and central rapidity ranges, with J/ψ mesons exhibiting nuclear modification factors below one, especially in proton-rich interactions.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, characterized by specific commutation relations that define the structure constants of a Lie algebra. By transforming the coordinates into linear differential operators in a commuting momentum space, we can reformulate this issue into an ordinary quantum problem. These operators, representing the coordinates $\hat x_a$, have a form $-i\hat D_a = -iE_{ab}(p)\partial /\partial p_b$, where $E_{ab}$ can be expressed as an infinite series over the deformation parameter $\theta$. The deformed Hamiltonian $\hat H$ describes the motion on corresponding group manifolds with sizes proportional to $\theta^{-1}$, whose metrics also appear in certain infinite series of $\theta$. The matrices $E_{ab}$ can be represented in simple forms for certain algebras like $su(2)$ and $u(N)$. The corresponding deformation matrices $E_{ab}$(θ) are readily obtainable and the related classical action can be approximated by treating the small parameters of the series. The obtained results indicate that the noncommutative quantum systems associated with Lie algebras have discrete spectrum with divergent energies, excluding the possibility of describing systems like the hydrogen atom based on noncommutative geometry. The obtained data also indicate that the noncommutative monopole problem cannot be solved within this framework. The obtained results support the idea that noncommutative geometry cannot be used to describe ordinary quantum

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to collect extensive training datasets at a single location. This has significant implications for the development of more reliable and accurate image analysis models in histopathology.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 72Gbit/s using the on-off keying technique, over a distance of 18.8km in a South China Sea submarine cable that lacks dispersion compensation.  Chromatic dispersion in this underwater cable causes four signal nulls in a 36GHz bandwidth, severely hindering BER performance. To address this issue, a decision feedback equalizer was initially applied with satisfactory results, however its effectiveness was impeded due to the occurrence of severe burst errors induced by the movement of the underwater cable. This equalization shortcoming was subsequently mitigated by incorporating a cascade of three main techniques into the decision feedback equalizer: optical filter function estimation, eye-contour based threshold setting, and partial updating of the memory, respectively. These enhancements led to a notable reduction in the BER, achieving a value of $3.48\times 10^{-3}$ after applying the optimized technique, a distance that could be covered in approximately 12.6km without any errors occurring. This research provides a theoretical framework for enhancing the spectral efficiency of future submarine fiber-optic communications systems.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which usually demands significant computational power. Nonetheless, research has indicated that compact time-dilation factors are crucial for excellent performance on time-series tasks. To achieve this, we propose a novel approach called Pruning in Time (PIT), an optimization technique that efficiently condenses TCNs by an order of magnitude with minimal accuracy loss. PIT successfully condenses TCNs with minimal dilation constraints, resulting in an architecture that performs exceptionally well on benchmark datasets like the MIMIC-III dataset, outperforming a heavily optimized TCN baseline by a margin of 8.5% in terms of low-mixture loss while matching the high-mixture loss for 1% model size.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are evident across different centralities and become more pronounced in more central collisions and in line with theoretical predictions. Furthermore, the fluctuations in magnitude are found to be similar to those observed in earlier, lower-energy LHC data, suggesting that the underlying properties of quark matter have not changed.

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for correspondence and canonicity across diverse semantic frameworks and signatures. These tools, specifically tailored to logics whose semantics rely on normal lattice expansions (DLEs), enable computation of first-order correspondents for inductive formulas using the algorithm ALBA. Conversely, our proposed method effectively employs ALBA's rules and algebraic language to reverse its computations in the case of DLE-Logics, thereby allowing the derivation of an inductive formula from its first-order correspondent.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the presence of missing values. We establish a framework where each data entry can be associated with a truth status: true, false, inconsistent, or undetermined. Furthermore, our framework facilitates an examination of the inherent properties of data in relation to specific functional dependencies and the consistency of data in relation to those dependencies. Key components of our framework include (a) methods to determine consistency in cases where data entries do not contain nulls, (b) techniques for identifying undetermined values by analyzing data entries with nulls, and (c) an examination of the conditions under which data entries with nulls can be determined as inconsistent. This research has implications for the development of strategies to handle data with nulls and functional dependencies and has been published in [1]. We invite the exchange of ideas and the exploration of further extensions to our framework.

This research introduces the time-varying Poisson autoregressive model (TPAR) to analyze and forecast count-based economic time series with non-stationarities in their mean values. The TPAR model is based on a time-varying parameter and a specific probability distribution for values above the threshold, allowing for the estimation of non-stationary conditional mean expectations. The likelihood function is used to estimate the model, and a Monte Carlo study confirms its effectiveness. Results from applying the model to real-world datasets show it outperforms existing alternatives.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
after witnessing a single demonstration. To achieve this, we use optimization
to locate the pose whose descriptor corresponds to that shown in a demonstration
video. NDFs are a more flexible alternative to traditional bounding box-based
representations, as they account for objects with holes, allow for grasping out
of binocular blindness, and capture rotational poses. Through experiments on the
Modl dataset, we find NDFs succeed in replicating tasks on objects with holes,
and from various rotational poses and Binocularly Hidden Grasps. Results show
our method generalizes well to new objects with 90% success rate on unseen test
objects from the same categories.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D prospects and participation opportunities for the SiD's development areas.

We present initial findings from the CAPOS survey, centered on the ancient open cluster Tonantzintla 2. Despite being easily resolvable with Hubble Space Telescope, the cluster's membership status remained unclear until the presentation of kinematical and stellar population data, which allowed for a distinct separation from surrounding field stars. A notable population of red giant stars was extracted from HST observations and was used to create a color-magnitude diagram characteristic of the cluster. This resulted in a well-defined sequence of probable members, which will serve as a reference for identifying cluster stars in upcoming APOGEE-GALACTIC Bulge Surveys. A separate paper will outline the survey's broader scope and objectives.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses certain challenges: locating specific content has become increasingly difficult, making it essential to prioritize reuse and clarity of comprehension. This thesis proposal outlines my research objectives, which focus on these concerns, as well as initial findings, which reveal that the Isabelle Archive exhibits characteristics typical of scale-free networks, as evidenced by the distribution of node in-degrees in its dependency graph.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have calculated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically, we found the edge singularity's location to be at $z = 1/2 - 1/(2d)$ for $d \geq 2$, which aligns with previous findings from field theory and renormalization group methods. Notably, we obtained a more general expression for $d = 1$, given by $z = 1/N$. Our research extends to universality classes beyond O(N), including Z2 and U(1) symmetries in 4d, where we determined the edge singularity's location at $z = 1/2 - 1/(2d)$.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a part of the Nishanth et al. algorithm for solving the Lasso problem.

Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field, involving electromagnetic systems characterized by  
thin, expansive, and minutely featured particles that can also vary spatially,  
temporally, and linearly.  To tackle this intricacy, researchers need to employ a  
unified approach, integrating theoretical design and analysis methods, supported  
by an established framework.  Recent breakthroughs, facilitated by Generalized  
Sheet Transition Conditions in combination with surface susceptibilities,  
now enable designers to develop intricate metasurfaces with unprecedented  
precision.  This chapter delves into computational modeling of these complex  
structures through GSTC-susceptibility methodology and underscores its pivotal  
role in the design of next-generation electromagnetic devices and technologies.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines a deep learning approach known as the Electron Correlation
Potential Neural Network (eCPNN), which can learn simplified potential functions
that accurately capture the intricate instantaneous relationships among electrons
within complex atomic systems. Trained in an unsupervised manner with constrained
data derived from Full Configuration Interaction one-electron density functions, the
eCPNN model effectively predicts total atomic energies with remarkable precision.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of approximately 0.8. Spanning nearly 1 billion light-years, this feature exhibits remarkable symmetry when viewed from space. It was discovered through a novel approach, using gravitational waves as a lens-delivery mechanism, thanks to the unique alignment of a distant supernova, a black hole merger, and Earth. Observations from the Hubble Space Telescope have provided the arc's intricate details, which display intricate patterns reminiscent of abstract art. The Giant Arc's unusual shape and massive size pose intriguing questions about the interplay of gravity that created it. It offers a unique opportunity to study how gravity distorts light through a complex web of galaxy clusters and foreground galaxies. The Giant Arc invites us to explore the intricate relationship between matter and light, much like the interplay between a painter's brush and the canvas it adorns.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad temperature range, the optical communication path can be determined, potentially allowing for the calculation of aerosol depth without relying on standard passbands. Researchers have experimented with an extensive database of 640 million observations from the AAVSO and the ASAS-SN, using multiple techniques including machine learning to determine the aerosol depth with a precision of 0.01-0.02, despite being outside the typical photometric precision. These findings suggest that using photometry from stars could be a reliable and cost-effective method for monitoring the atmosphere.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using a single image has gained significant interest, primarily utilizing convolutional neural networks (CNN). Research has concentrated on direct methods that predict the pose in a single step but often struggle with high dimensionality and limited training data. In contrast, indirect methods break the task into manageable sub-tasks, such as object detection and pose estimation from a 2D projection. However, these methods have inconsistencies in coordinate systems. To address these challenges, we propose an alternative framework, where the task is split across multiple expert networks that learn to recognize unique features in a object-specific coordinate system. For training and maintenance, we introduce a novel training scheme based on correspondence learning with a consistent coordinate system and minimal object-specific assumptions. To circumvent the issue of varying projections, we propose a new approach called projection grouping, where similar projections are grouped together and learned implicitly. The framework is evaluated on three challenging datasets (LPD, COPE, and IIT-Radar Pose, but only LPD and COPE used in training and testing setup as described in original research) and demonstrates improved performance (+4.34 and +4.56 average accuracy, respectively) in comparison with state-of-the-art indirect methods and our initial prototype.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuity formation within materials. Bond-based Peridynamics, despite its modeling restrictions, has become a widely used approach in numerical simulations because of its ease of implementation and intuitive connection to real-world physics. This paper delves into a comprehensive exploration of bond-based peridynamics, focusing on the mathematical foundations, implicit and semi-implicit numerical solution methods, and a range of numerical techniques including contact mechanics, fracture propagation, and fluid dynamics. A unique aspect of this paper is the examination of the role of nonlocality in fluid dynamics, an area where bond-based peridynamics surprisingly shows potential despite being a non-Newtonian model. Building on previous research, we propose an explicit solution algorithm for bond-based PD equations, and investigate the incorporation of thermal effects into bond-based peridynamics. Finally, we investigate the incorporation of thermal effects into bond-based peridynamics, and investigate the incorporation of thermal effects into bond-based peridynamics.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can jointly estimate multiple
inverse covariance matrices, as shown in Danaher (2013) and Tomasi (2018). The
GGLasso package supports the resolution of diverse formulations and notable
subcases like Graphical Lasso with latent variables, Group, and Fused Graphical Lasso.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic approximation techniques, variance reduction strategies, and implicit-explicit numerical solutions. A novel approach has been proposed to achieve efficient and robust configurational sampling in molecular dynamics simulations, involving the application of a specific implicit-explicit numerical solution to the Langevin equation. This method ensures conservation of physical properties such as energy, minimizes artificial added noise, and eliminates negative configurational energy states that arise in explicit time integration methods. The proposed algorithm exhibits superior performance compared to alternative implicit numerical solutions, particularly for large time steps and complex biomolecules. Moreover, it demonstrates comparable performance to the widely used GROMACs stochastic integrator, but with improved robustness and efficiency. The method has been successfully tested on a variety of model systems and large biomolecular simulations.

Numerical relativity simulations allow us to study how binary black hole mergers interact with their surroundings. However, these simulations significantly struggle with handling a large number of particles, a challenge that grows when considering the long-term impact of gravitational waves on matter. As General Relativity and the Large-Scale Structure of the Universe suggest that dark matter should respond to gravitational waves similarly to regular matter, it's essential to investigate the validity of this assumption through numerical simulations. To explore this, we conducted a set of simulations for binary black hole mergers, comparing regular matter environments to dark matter environments with the same total mass as the matter case. The simulations revealed that in wave dark matter environments, the tidal accretion rate of the smaller binary black hole is overestimated by up to 25% due to the lack of scattering that occurs in the matter case. Furthermore, we found that the accuracy of our simulations is consistent with a proposed equation that takes into account the fraction of matter bound to the more massive binary component. As a result, we anticipate that future simulations incorporating the behavior of dark matter in gravitational waves will become necessary.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The inner point is capable of moving in two ways, with rotational movement influenced by both elasticity and friction. A detailed analysis in a Hilbert space reveals how the spectrum's asymptotic distribution and structure evolve. It demonstrates that specific eigenvector characteristics form a complete and orthonormal basis. Consequently, we derive the exponential stability of the associated semigroup directly. Notably, we show that under these connectivity conditions, stability is guaranteed even in the absence of elasticity along the edges.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to increase the detection area of sensitive devices and improve resolution but discovered these lenses introduced image distortion. This problem was investigated and a new lens material called Stycast 1090SI was proposed as an alternative. The acoustic properties of this novel material were examined alongside PMMA to determine its feasibility. Computational simulations and practical tests using two different materials, PMMA and Stycast 1090SI, showed both materials significantly enhance the detection capabilities of sensitive devices. Notably, the Stycast lens exhibited lower levels of distortion compared to the PMMA lens, which could have implications for photoacoustic tomography technology.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach distinguishes itself by allowing for the flexible inclusion of inter-layer connections in a future expansion of the method.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative design that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them in an interpretable way. To train this model, we utilize real-world camera data transformed into raw images through a realistic process, mimicking real-world camera functions. In contrast to conventional methods that assume the availability of a high-quality image, our approach can recover severely degraded images from raw data, outperforming existing methods according to PSNR and SSIM metrics.

Recently, we generated the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra using deformed Poisson brackets, 
which effectively replicate the Fock coordinate transformation. This transformation 
corresponds to a de Sitter spacetime. In this study, we formulate the Dirac equation within 
$R$-Minkowski spacetime and establish that it is analogous to the Dirac equation defined 
within the de Sitter spacetime, described by its conformally flat metric. We then propose 
a novel strategy to solve the Dirac equation within the de Sitter spacetime by adopting 
the Schr\"{o}dinger picture.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal relationships between the variables involved. At the core of this process is the application of a suite of methods for detecting causal relationships from data, including those developed by Pantaroyo et al. and Spirtes et al. The framework is showcased through its application to a simulation scenario and a real-world dataset.

This research investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules describing when the splash dome closes ("pinch-off time") generally hold for both slow-moving and fast-moving spheres, yet require further refinement, especially in the middle speed range. In fact, at mid-range speeds, pinch-off times relate differently to fluid dynamics principles than they do at either low or high speeds, indicating that increased pressures inside the formed cavity play a significant role. In addition, our analysis reveals that the pressure increase is sufficient to prolong pinch-off times by a pinching frequency-based amount, beyond what is caused by water rushing into the cavity. As a result, we propose a more comprehensive theory that takes into account both internal pressure and the interplay between the sphere and water during pinch-off. This new understanding is consistent with data collected during our water entry experiments using high-speed cameras and pressure sensors attached to spheres entering the water at mid-range speeds.

We investigate a comprehensive set of symmetries characterized by Kähler monodromy, present in Type IIB Calabi-Yau compactifications and analyze their implications on the Type IIB effective field theory. Our research reveals that this symmetry group dictates stringent constraints on the features of the effective field theory, specifically requiring the presence of peculiar $\alpha'$-corrected terms known as generalized theta-terms that break this symmetry. These terms are found to be essential for ensuring that the monodromy symmetry remains intact down to energies influenced by the Calabi-Yau volume, and we establish a connection between the generalized theta-terms and a related group of transformations defined by the mirror symmetry. Our findings suggest that the charged states associated with these terms possess non-trivial, intrinsically defined properties. Furthermore, we establish a distinction between coherent and non-coherent states, demonstrating that the action of the monodromy symmetry group differs significantly between these two circumstances.

Mobile device owners frequently need to balance security and convenience when sharing their device with others, such as giving their phone to a friend to quickly look up directions, taking a photo, or making a brief phone call. This paper introduces the concept of a one-time, isolated "sprint" on a device, where a user grants limited access to their phone's operating system and hardware for a brief period. Building on previous work involving prolonged collaborations, this research focuses on isolated "sprints" to understand how to minimize trust requirements by optimizing performance, user experience, and security for time-sensitive, low-risk scenarios. A novel performance model and a trust-aware design framework are presented to address this challenge. A user-friendly, customizable interface is also proposed to facilitate seamless interaction between application developers and the research community. An "enclave" hardware and software platform was developed to test and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed design. Favorable results from user feedback and performance evaluations show that trusted time-sensitive applications can be efficiently designed using the proposed framework and system.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where an adaptive adversary intentionally manipulates rewards and transition probabilities. The adversary's influence is confined to no more than an $\epsilon$ fraction of all training episodes. Notably, this attack model surpasses previously considered methods. We established a key finding that no reinforcement learning algorithm can discover an optimal policy with a lower error rate than $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{\epsilon T})$ under these circumstances. We devised a robust reinforcement learning framework that leverages a least squares algorithm for value function estimation and an adversarial policy iteration method. Theoretical performance evaluations indicate that the proposed framework achieves a robust error rate of $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{\epsilon T})$. Moreover, we conducted explicit calculations for several standard reinforcement learning settings. Furthermore, our results demonstrate that efficient robust reinforcement learning is feasible when the corruption is relatively mild. Nevertheless, we established that reinforcement learning becomes computationally intractable when the corruption is severe. The problem of robust reinforcement learning has been addressed through various methods such as designing robust value function estimators and robust policy evaluation algorithms. We proposed a robust reinforcement learning framework that combines a robust value function estimator and an adversarial policy iteration method. The proposed framework has a robust error rate of $\tilde{O}(\sqrt{\epsilon T})$.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as quantum artificial lattices, is on the cusp of a breakthrough, thanks in part to the promising results obtained from two-dimensional materials systems. To further advance this field, researchers are seeking to establish a level of control over the motion of charge carriers in a way that is both precise and adaptable. One crucial aspect of this control involves the ability to manipulate a carrier's spin, often achieved through the application of an external magnetic field. However, this approach has limitations, primarily due to the difficulty of scaling it up for larger systems. In a groundbreaking experiment, scientists have successfully self-assembled monolayers using heavy-metal molecules that can interact with a specific point on a graphene lattice, resulting in the creation of a self-consistent field that governs the motion of both electrons and holes. By leveraging this interaction, the researchers were able to induce a self-binding effect known as a dark exciton and demonstrated the ability to transfer an exciton's energy to an adjacent site through quantum fluctuations. What's more, they were able to employ this self-binding feature to manipulate an electron and a hole as if they were a single entity and even achieved control over an array of excitons through resonance. Furthermore, the findings indicate that this self-binding effect can enhance the likelihood of a carrier's spin being transferred to another location and could potentially be utilized to develop more intricate quantum states and better control the motion of charge carriers.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two types of translations and one glide symmetry in a 2D space. Our model incorporates nearest-neighbor hopping with different energies, except for one exceptional site that shares high energy with three neighboring sites. We discovered isolated Dirac points within the non-symmorphic lattice's band structure, located in the center of the Brillouin zone, around the high-energy site's local zone. These Dirac points are surrounded by a rosetta-shaped area, characterized by quasi-one-dimensional flat bands with varying Chern numbers. The number of flat bands and the Chern number change as we move from one isolated Dirac point to another, according to a Chern number that's determined by the lattice's glide symmetry. A suitable on-site potential can merge isolated Dirac points into a ring featuring tunable flat bands with non-trivial Chern phases. Additionally, we propose an experimental setup using a graphene-hBN system with an external electric field to replicate and study this model.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. These findings demonstrate that SPCCSs possess abundant non-classical behavior, thereby conferring a quantum advantage for executing various technological tasks.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using connected substructures and employs linear regression within the NP-hard problem of constraint satisfaction to determine the specific chemical components that make up a polymer. To overcome this difficulty, a new approach has been proposed that divides the problem into two more manageable parts of determining the connected substructure and placement within a polymer framework. This approach has been successfully demonstrated on a reduced polymer compound library but faces challenges with larger-scale compounds and needs further optimization for its application.

This paper presents a unified approach to addressing certain complex optimization challenges. Problems of control, estimation, and system reconfiguration can be solved using a unified framework based on direct transcription methods. A specific problem is highlighted where the goal is to deliver sufficient ventilation to two COVID-19 patients sharing a ventilation room by dispersing virus-laden aerosols. The problem is modeled and solved using the NLP form of the direct transcription method. Comparative solutions are obtained using Newton's and Levenberg Marquardt methods.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these challenges, doctors often rely on additional information when treating cancer patients, which slows down the treatment process. In order to accelerate and improve precision of the diagnosis, a non-invasive method to automatically detect and outline tumors in the esophagus from CT scans is proposed here. We developed a novel, automatic segmentation algorithm based on deep learning called the Dilated Dense Attention Unet, which significantly outperformed existing methods according to expert radiologists who evaluated and tested it with real-world data.

The expense of investing in new oil fields through drilling can be significant, thus the importance of geosteering technology in minimizing costs cannot be overstated. Geosteering involves continuously interpreting well log data to make informed decisions about adjusting the direction and depth of well placement in real-time or near real-time. Despite its effectiveness, this technology's adoption is limited by the time-consuming nature of traditional, manual well log interpretation methods. To overcome this hurdle, we propose an automated framework utilizing multiple models and ensembles to efficiently provide accurate and timely interpretations of well log data. This framework leverages point-scatter process models to model facies based on well log data, then applies Gaussian process regression models to accurately interpret and recover unidentified well log data from limited core measurements. By combining the results from multiple models and Monte Carlo trials, the framework produces data noise-aware facies interpretations and associated uncertainties, which can guide real-time or near real-time decision-making during well placement. We demonstrate the performance of this automated framework by testing it on a genuine well log data set from the Norwegian Continental Shelf.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER focuses on the recognition of entities within other entities. Although numerous studies have been conducted on this topic, the task remains challenging due to the intricate relationships between overlapping entities and the need to consider them as a whole. In this paper, a novel approach to nested NER is proposed, incorporating a holistic understanding of the text. We treat the entities as a single unit and aim to understand their overall meaning. This approach is implemented through the proposed HSP model, which establishes a complex structure to capture the relationships between entities and the text as a whole. We also introduce the Nested Labeled Graph Transformation (NLGT) model, a nested NER model that uses a bidirectional transformer encoder to create a graph representing the text's structure and entity relationships. However, our primary contribution lies in a simple yet effective model called the Simple Nested Graph Transducer (SNGT), which achieves superior performance compared to existing methods according to our experiments.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic problems, such as enumerating objects in higher-dimensional spaces using values from specific algebraic structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties as a reference. We look at curves that are defined by equations that are smooth, specifically those that are used to determine tangency in a specific way, and how they relate to other curves that have the same general form but have different tangent properties. We express the relationship between these curves using values from specific algebraic structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties as a reference. We focus on objects such as lines that pass through specific points in a way that are related to these curves, particularly those that do not satisfy the required tangency in a specific way. We develop a method to calculate or estimate the number of these objects using values from specific algebraic structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties as a reference, based on the properties of these structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties as a reference. We look at how these structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties as a reference change and how that affects the number of these objects. Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To enhance accuracy, we utilize a method previously employed in lognormal shadowing models to calculate the standard deviation of RSSI readings from individual sensors. We differentiate between static and dynamic shadowing influences and employ specific formulas accordingly. The proposed method is tested under realistic conditions using a custom simulation tool and shows improved performance compared to conventional methods. Results indicate that the standard deviation of dynamic shadowing effects has a significant impact on location accuracy and must be considered in such applications.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, multiple variations of human-generated captions exist for the same image, it is essential to consider if a system's performance is a genuine indicator of its capabilities or rather an artifact of its preference for certain descriptions over others. This concern is the primary motivation for our research, which aims to investigate the relationship between system performance and the nature of human-generated data. Two main findings emerge from our study: performance is largely insensitive to the specific dataset of human-generated descriptions used; furthermore, a notable disparity exists between human-generated captions collected through crowdsourcing and those naturally posted online with respect to length, where the latter exhibits a more notable deviation. As such, our research cautions against relying solely on human-generated data collected through crowdsourcing for systematic evaluations of image description systems.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties such as high dielectric values, low loss tangents, and optical characteristics. For electronic application, where substrate material is Ta$_2$O$_5$, it is crucial to identify the most stable crystalline form among the numerous variants of this oxide. Previous research employed empirical approaches to determine the most stable form, but those methods lacked precision. Our study employed a first-principles simulation method to investigate the fundamental characteristics of Ta$_2$O$_5$ and employed a Monte Carlo algorithm to examine all possible polymorphs at the melting point, effectively identifying the most thermodynamically stable form. The results show that Ta$_2$O$_5$ has a stable $\beta$-Ta2O5 structure at room temperature and has a significant bandgap of approximately 3.6 eV. The study also provides a theoretical basis for the calculation of a variety of Ta$_2$O$_5$ properties, including lattice vibrations, an average bulk modulus of around 103 GPa, and a specific heat capacity that aligns with general expectations.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to personal factors, such as information literacy, and social media influences, but ignored a third aspect: the impact of the physical separation of Americans in geographical regions. We tested the significance of this phenomenon, known as "The Big Sort," on online misinformation spread. We analyzed more than 8 million Reddit comments from news articles spanning four years and found that misinformation did not spread primarily through the features of the Reddit platform, but rather was linked to user population size in each state, following a supply-and-demand model. Furthermore, variations in misinformation dissemination were explained by local personality traits and cultural characteristics rather than economic, social, or political conditions. In areas where residents are less diligent in nature, and cultures place little emphasis on adherence to norms, we found increased circulation of all news, including credible sources.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient, and user-friendly detection mechanism for identifying unexpected occurrences in real-time data streams. By acknowledging the limitations of traditional methods like Hoeffding bounds and the challenges of developing effective and easy-to-use detection systems, we present a novel approach based on a geometric interpretation of the well-known Kullback-Leibler divergence. To demonstrate its performance, the proposed method was tested against a widely used algorithm for event detection and showed comparable results in simulated environments.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, it is crucial to analyze their underlying content and pattern. This study initiates a first look at audios accompanying robotic manipulative task demonstrations through a learned representation of the audio data. We demonstrate that audio data contains valuable information to enhance learning and maintain consistency with the visual data by undergoing similar transformations during retargeting and domain adaptation. Furthermore, we introduce a simple framework to assess the semantic content of audio data and found it to be more robust than other methods. We also observed that audio data contains valuable non-semantic information with a frequency spectrum resembling that of the frequency spectrum produced by the robotic actions.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore potential applications of the algorithm, illustrating its use in deriving formulas by utilizing the underlying proof of correctness.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and requiring a more detailed understanding of interacting theories. A promising approach involves linking the geometric action of a charge in spacetime with the operator algebra of a conformal field theory, achieved through Wightman two-point correlations. However, this geometric method encounters difficulties when applied to non-trivial self-energy scenarios due to the presence of divergent universal terms in correlation functions. Recently, a proposal was made to overcome this challenge by focusing on relative correlations of an operator with the identity, thereby separating universal and operator-specific components and facilitating a more direct connection between geometric and algebraic properties of a conformal field theory. Building on this proposal, a framework is established where the Euler-Arnold equation is applied to define a geometric complexity functional for a conformal field theory, while relative correlations are shown to satisfy the Euler-Arnold equation. The derivation relies on an expansion of two-point correlations in terms of a geometric series and the use of a conformal algebra representation.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. In this paper, we outline a cutting-edge, fully automated testing framework that leverages natural language processing techniques to efficiently evaluate the functionality and usability of conversational agents. The framework can handle multiple dialogue management systems and integrate various usability and functionality assessment tools. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework by conducting a methodological evaluation of several popular conversational agents. The source code of this testing framework has been made publicly available on GitHub.

Using a sophisticated mathematical model known as the Fisher information matrix, it's possible to estimate the measurement uncertainties $\sigma_M$ associated with detecting a hypothetical "Planet X" by analyzing its impact on the gravitational field of the known planets. Based on existing measurements from the Juno, Cassini, and Mars-orbiting spacecraft, a 1-sigma uncertainty of $\sigma_M \approx 1.1$ Earth masses can be achieved with a 95% confidence level. This represents the minimum mass of Planet X that could be detected with certainty. When modeling is limited to Juno data, the uncertainty is higher at $\sigma_M \approx 2.3$ Earth masses. It's also possible to estimate the uncertainty $\sigma_d$ associated with determining the orbit of Planet X. Based on all available data, a 1-sigma uncertainty of $\sigma_d \approx 20^\circ$ can be estimated with a 95% confidence level. This could significantly affect the likelihood of detecting Planet X through its gravitational influence on the orbits of the outer planets in the solar system.

Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance. Unlike existing approaches which rely on bilingual corpora for TM and employ source-side similarity searches, our proposed framework leverages monolingual data and retrieves memories in a cross-lingual manner. Notably, our framework offers two significant advantages: firstly, it enables vast amounts of monolingual data to be incorporated into TM; secondly, both the memory retriever and the NMT model can be jointly optimised. Experimental results indicate that the proposed method achieves substantial gains in performance and outperforms TM-augmented NMT baselines even when utilizing bilingual TM. Furthermore, our model exhibits impressive ability to learn topic structures from monolingual data, thereby facilitating the learning of rare and idiomatic expressions.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Pseudo-Riemannian Signature Change theory. To facilitate the detection of these patterns, we employed a novel method that leverages machine learning to automatically identify and extract them from the CMB data. Our analysis of the Planck and Atacama Cosmology Telescope data sets revealed statistical evidence for the presence of these patterns, and the distribution of features in the CMB sky aligns with predictions made by the theory. Furthermore, the features are concentrated in regions associated with the Milky Way's influence and other nearby galaxy clusters, and exhibit a correlation with the direction of these gravitational fields. Our findings suggest that the presence of these patterns could be a distinctive fingerprint of the theory, and warrant further investigation through modified cosmological simulations and potential connections with other related theories.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that rely on average operations for calculating prototypes often struggle due to the influence of outliers. This research proposes a new, effective framework that utilizes an episodic prototype generator module to create more representative prototypes from limited support data, reducing the impact of outliers and resulting in the incorporation of all support data. Moreover, the framework is highly adaptable and can be applied across various metrics used for classification. Evaluations on three popular few-shot learning datasets demonstrate that our method not only outperforms the current state-of-the-art but also offers greater versatility and versatility in learning new classes.

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention as a means to enhance user-based and item-based recommendations through leveraging knowledge and resources from multiple, separately managed domains. Although numerous algorithms have been proposed to achieve cross-domain recommendations, there remains a notable absence of frameworks that can handle multiple domains by providing a unified aspect preference learning framework. In an effort to address this gap, we introduce a novel framework called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) that can effectively recommend items by combining the preferences of users across multiple domains. Within the MSDCR framework, we propose an Enhanced Computationally-Integrated Aspect Preference Learning (ECA-PIAL) model that accurately determines a user's aspect preferences by gathering and aggregating partial information from across multiple domains. Furthermore, we develop a distributed and flexible framework called Multi-Domain Recommendation Framework (MDRF) that efficiently and easily enables the implementation of the MSDCR framework across multiple domains. Through extensive numerical experiments and practical evaluations, we demonstrate the efficacy and versatility of the MSDCR framework.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This work introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications that can provide significant improvements in processing speed and memory consumption. The proposed method demonstrates a marked improvement in problem-solving efficiency when compared to more conventional and complex conic formulations.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, enabling numerous applications including clinical trials, brain damage assessment, and neurological disorder diagnosis. Although existing methods can detect anomaly images from a large dataset, they typically require processing each dataset individually due to significantly varying scanning parameters, field strengths, and resolution sizes. In this study, we propose a diverse dataset consisting of 150,000 3D brain MRI slices from 1,000 3D volumes, spanning 17 distinct scanning protocols, to test the generalization capabilities of our proposed method. We extract 12 features of varying complexity to assess their effectiveness in predicting in-pocket MRI anomalies. Our results indicate that a relatively simple feature set is sufficient to generalize across MRI data from different scanners and protocols, achieving a 90% accuracy rate. Notably, our method surpasses the performance of a state-of-the-art anomaly detection model while requiring significantly fewer computational resources.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory Module (DC PMM) has introduced a new memory technology that provides high capacity, low latency, and endless endurance. It exists at the boundary between memory and storage, offering flexible usage options. This storage technology can be viewed as a large pool of non-volatile memory, accessible through the Memory Channel Interface, and is managed by the operating system in a similar manner to traditional RAM. However, its high cost and limited capacity currently restrict its appeal to small numbers of high-performance applications, such as in-memory databases, scientific simulations, and data analytics. To make the Optane DC PMM more accessible for general-purpose use, we have investigated its performance in various standard benchmarks, including PHP, Java, stream processing, small bioinformatics applications, and several fields of scientific simulation, and found it to be a viable and efficient option.

The Motivation Dynamics framework is expanded upon to accommodate the interactions of multiple autonomous agents meeting a target at a specific time. A self-encapsulating rationale is introduced, where the controller is assured to cooperatively achieve the desired meeting time with no need for explicit communication or a common global perspective. Building upon previous findings, the paper demonstrates that a diverse range of collision-free paths can be generated naturally, emerging from the interaction of the Motivation Dynamics system. Numerical simulations and a corresponding experimental setup both validate the proposed concept.

This paper investigates the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We examined the antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic configurations in GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3, finding that the latter has a higher energy compared to the former in all three compounds. Notably, CmSn3 exhibits a higher energy configuration similar to GdSn3 and GdxCm1-xSn3, indicating these compounds share analogous electronic structures. Additionally, both GdSn3 and CmSn3 demonstrate a stable tetragonal crystal structure, whereas the series GdxCm1-xSn3 adopts this structure only at x=0.25 and $0.5$, transforming into a stable orthorhombic structure at x=0.75. These findings suggest the possibility of synthesizing these half-metallic ferromagnets using the post-annealing method.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental properties of matter and modifying the force that governs baryon and lepton interactions. Researchers have previously explored similar theories, but the bilepton model offers a comprehensive framework that makes specific predictions for new baryons and mesons based on symmetry and fundamental property changes. By applying group theoretical calculations, the paper identifies 6 new quark combinations, 19 new baryons, 19 new mesons, and 2 diquark objects that fit within this extended framework. Additionally, the paper focuses on the new baryons and mesons that could be detected with existing or near-future experimental setups, particularly in particle collision experiments like the Large Hadron Collider.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws for Bn similar to those of the symmetric group. This standardization also aligns with the group's action, giving rise to exchange laws that reflect Bn's geometric structure.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a 3.6-sigma significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we constrained galactic halo properties, including the mass-to-light ratio, which is in line with previous cosmological studies. By accounting for this lensing effect, we found a 4.3-sigma significance and were able to estimate the dark energy parameter omega_de at 0.703 +/- 0.038, which is consistent with other methods.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on Hilbert space-based functional analysis, operator theory, and stochastic analysis has been recapitulated within the lecture notes and further relevant references are included. 

The concluding chapter covers the pathwise approach.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on the creation of reliable channels for coherent control of a target atom or molecule. In the field of quantum cryptography, for example, coherent control of a silicon-based "qubit" might be achieved through interaction with a neutral hydrogen-like defect in the silicon, specifically the Si-F centre system, via a silicon-based photon. While defects in silicon offer several advantages, such as low loss transmission and the availability of highly precise fabrication techniques, there is a significant lack of understanding about the Si-T centre system. This study investigates the Si-T centre by combining optical detection of magnetic resonance with time-domain spectroscopy, allowing it to determine key properties including the g factor, zero-photon energy, and a range of related parameters. Findings show that a Si-T centre in a <100> silicon crystal has unique characteristics which may make it suitable for the coherent control of a target channel. Moreover, this study demonstrates the potential for a strong connection between a Si-T centre and a silicon photonic mode.

MRI technology is a non-invasive diagnostic tool that allows radiologists to examine the interior of the body with minimal disruption.  Advanced imaging capabilities, particularly high-resolution scans, enable precise visualization of the body's internal structures.  Through automated image processing methods, medical professionals can efficiently obtain detailed information about the body's physiological and pathological conditions.  This research focuses on automated tumor detection in MRI images using a variety of processing techniques, including thresholding, Fourier transform, and edge detection methods, to be specific, Otsu's method, the discrete Fourier transform, and Canny edge detection.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an innovative algebraic framework for generating functions and symbolic evaluation functions, allowing us to derive $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$. Our findings demonstrate intriguing connections with circulant matrices and Galois fields, while showcasing the potential for $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ to be applied in computationally efficient contexts.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs present a significant challenge for discovering exoplanets, as their stellar activity masks the signals from these celestial bodies. This problem necessitates a thorough understanding of how to minimize the noise from stellar activity to ensure effective planet detection. In this study, we utilized least-squares deconvolution on a random sample of low-resolution spectra of AD Leo to separate the light variations caused by stellar activity. We compared two approaches to selecting spectral lines: a systematic approach based on cross-correlation with planetary signals and a random method. For the systematic approach, we chose 695 lines with strong correlation to no correlation with planetary signals and applied LSD to these lines. For the random approach, we randomly selected 100, 300, and 500 lines from the total of 695 lines with strong correlation to no correlation with planetary signals and applied LSD to these lines. We discovered that the random approach yielded similar noise levels to the systematic approach when we randomly selected 300 lines out of 695 lines. These findings demonstrate that both methods can minimize noise caused by stellar activity, potentially enhancing the detection of exoplanets.

This research paper proposes a pair of methods for designing a flexible and efficient data collection process in Wireless Sensor Networks. Following data being generated in sensors, an on-demand data transfer mechanism is triggered, requiring a node to be appointed as the head of collection. To achieve this, a method for link quality estimation between nodes is presented, taking into account the energy constraints of sensors. A second method is presented for estimating distances between nodes, enabling a data head node to be chosen efficiently. A hybrid protocol is presented, incorporating these methods, and its performance is evaluated against other protocols. Results show that the proposed protocol achieves high data delivery rates and minimizes energy consumption.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
This study categorizes object detectors into three groups based on context usage:
one that doesn't use context by isolating the scene, one that uses partial context,
and one that uses full context without isolation.
To evaluate the effect of context on each deep detector, we propose the ContextEvaluation metric, which assesses context impact by comparing results of models with and without context.
To test our metric, we created a ContextEvaluation dataset that includes 6000 images with labels for whether the context aids in object recognition.
The context effect is shown to differ significantly among the three groups of object detectors.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$, within the bounded domain $\Omega$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $x$ contains the origin with smooth boundary, and for a certain condition $\beta\in [0,2)$; here $m$ denotes a function that belongs to Kirchhoff type, $f_i$ behave like $e^{\beta s^2}$, and there is a function $h_i\in \left(\big(H^1_0(\Omega)\big)^*,\|\cdot\|_*\right)$. By making use of a singular Trudinger-Moser inequality for a small positive value $\varepsilon$, multiple solutions can be obtained.

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic covering property (SCP) or the strong Rayleigh property (SRP). Our findings concerning SCP measures yield new subgaussian inequalities of a bounded-difference type, surpassing earlier results by providing stronger bounds. For SRP measures, our inequalities improve upon existing weak-difference inequalities. Additionally, we prove a strong-difference inequality for both SCP and SRP measures. These results extensions apply to nonnegative functions as well. This research builds upon prior works by Berman, Reidel, Reitzner, and Rytsov.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, we establish theorems enabling the comparison of crystalline and \'etale cohomologies with torsion coefficients for smooth schemes $X$ over $R$.

This research investigates the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering where hadron pairs' transverse momentum is not considered. Specifically, we focus on why there is a cosine asymmetry in the azimuthal angle between hadron pairs' planes when spin is doubled. Building on existing research, we examine how the color dance of initial partons contributes to this phenomenon. We demonstrate that significant contributions arise from interactions between the helicity and twist-3 quark and gluon distributions within the proton. In order to observe this effect, we found that a large scale of the order $k_T^2$ must be substantial, which in turn requires a considerable resolution in $k_T$. We further explored how this impact is felt across different components of the amplitude and found that the impact is primarily due to the helicity-twist-3 quark and gluon distributions within the proton. In order to observe this effect, we found that a large scale of the order $k_T^2$ must be substantial, which in turn requires a considerable resolution in $k_T$. This contribution can be examined through the helicity-twist-3 quark and gluon distributions within the proton. In order to observe this effect, we found that a large scale of the order $k_T^2$ must be substantial, which in turn requires a considerable resolution in $k_T$.

We've established recently, much like our work on Deformed Special Relativity, that Fock's coordinate transformation can be developed from a novel, deformed form of the Poisson brackets.  Utilizing this approach, we successfully obtained the associated momentum transformation, which preserves the four-dimensional relationship between momentum and space, p_{\mu} x^{\mu}.  Building upon these findings, we have derived the first quantization equation for a free particle, resulting in a hypergeometric-like spectrum when applying Deformed Special Relativity.  Furthermore, we have obtained the wave equation in curved space-time, remarkably retrieving the mass laplace-beltrami equation in the limit of small deformations.  Interestingly, we have observed that the hypergeometric-like spectrum may indicate a minimum length, or that it merely presents alternative quantization, leading to a minimum observable length.  Additionally, we have investigated the relationship between our approach and the standard treatment of particle propagation in the de Sitter space-time.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach, where the Wikipedia database is hierarchically divided into layered graphs to extract entity features and learn entity representations. By combining the extracted information with a lightweight ranking method, this framework effectively suggests related entities to users on Wikipedia. We evaluate our approach through both offline and real-world online tests, demonstrating that our embeddings and recommendations exhibit desirable quality and user engagement. Furthermore, this work showcases an interesting application where entities from the Wikipedia knowledge base can be recommended in various Yahoo! applications, such as news and search.
